technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline: Java 17, Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, Maven-based multi-module build on the existing XD codebase.

U1: Implement a custom Spring Data repository backed by a local RocksDB-based off-heap state store (Kafka Streams-style), with a compacted Kafka changelog topic per store for durability and startup restore.

U2: Implement an offset manager that gates Kafka consumer offset commits on successful module-producer acknowledgements (producer send callbacks), with batch-size and time-interval flush thresholds and async commit.

U3: Implement intelligent state flushing using a write-behind strategy with dirty-record tracking; state and changelog writes are flushed only after corresponding producer acknowledgement, treating the changelog as the write-ahead log.

U4: Build the CoAP source module on Eclipse Californium (CoAP server endpoint), mapping CoAP CON/NON and Observe notifications plus content-formats onto XD bus messages; follow the existing XD module contract for sources.
U5: Produce reference documentation in the project's existing Asciidoc format with complete configuration-property tables and examples for the deployment manifest properties file.
U6: Secure HDFS/Sqoop access via Kerberos using keytab + JAAS and Hadoop UserGroupInformation.doAs; validate against a MiniKDC-backed kerberized HDFS mini-cluster.

U7: Implement the Java Diego receptor client over the Receptor REST API (Tasks, DesiredLRPs, ActualLRPs, Cells, Domains) using Spring WebClient, with DTO model classes, OAuth/bearer token authentication, and structured error handling.

U8: Implement the Boot-based ModuleRunner as an executable Spring Boot application that launches and wires modules without xd-containers, using @ConfigurationProperties binding, and complete the remaining deployment properties (instance count, resource limits, module-level overrides).
Testing strategy: JUnit 5, embedded/Testcontainers Kafka, Californium test client, WireMock stubs for the Receptor API, and MiniKDC for Kerberos; integration tests run in CI.
assumptions: A single experienced developer (proficient in Spring, Kafka, Hadoop, and CF/Diego) performs all work; estimates are effort in work-hours, not elapsed duration.
The existing XD codebase, module/container infrastructure, message bus abstraction, and CI/build system are available and functional.
The Diego Receptor REST API specification is available and stable; testing uses recorded responses/mocks rather than a live Diego deployment.
The CoAP module is a source only (receives data); DTLS-secured CoAP is out of scope for this increment, with configuration hooks left for it.
Kerberos support covers single-realm keytab authentication only; cross-realm and credential delegation are out of scope.
No UI work is required; documentation targets the existing reference-docs toolchain.
Estimates include design, implementation, unit and integration testing, code review rework, and documentation for each story; they exclude meetings, support duties, and waiting time.
Each activity estimate is a single most-likely value with no additional contingency padding.

activities.activity_name: Increment requirements analysis and architecture design
activities.activity_description: Analyze all eight user stories, define the overall increment architecture, interfaces between new components and the existing XD runtime, and produce design notes.
Set up JDK 17 / Spring 6 baseline, embedded/Testcontainers Kafka, MiniKDC kerberized HDFS mini-cluster, CoAP tooling (Californium), and WireMock stubs for the Receptor API.
Design the Spring Data repository abstraction over a local off-heap state store with Kafka changelog persistence, including topic layout, partitioning, and restore semantics.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Implement local off-heap state store
activities.activity_description: Implement the RocksDB-based off-heap key/value store with serialization, iterators, and metrics for local data affinity.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Implement changelog sync and restore
activities.activity_description: Implement changelog production on writes and consumer-based restore of the local store on startup/failover from the compacted changelog topic.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Implement Spring Data repository integration
activities.activity_description: Bridge the state store to a Spring Data repository API (CRUD/query methods) usable from stateful stream processing modules.
Unit tests plus integration tests against embedded Kafka covering write/read, restore after restart, and failure scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Design intelligent offset flush strategy
activities.activity_description: Design correlation between consumed offsets and module-producer acknowledgements, flush thresholds, and error handling.
Implement offset tracking gated on producer send callbacks, with batch/time-based asynchronous offset commits to Kafka.
Tests for ack-gated committing, at-least-once semantics on producer failure, and flush threshold behavior with embedded Kafka.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Design intelligent state flush strategy
activities.activity_description: Design write-behind state flushing tied to producer acknowledgements, dirty-record tracking, and recovery behavior.
Implement flushing of local state and changelog writes only after successful module-producer acknowledgements, including failure rollback paths.
Tests for flush-on-ack behavior, consistency after crash/restart, and interaction with the U1 store and U2 offset manager.
Design the CoAP source module contract: resource endpoints, content-format to message mapping, and configuration properties.
Implement the Californium-based CoAP server endpoint (CON/NON, Observe), payload conversion, and emission onto the XD message bus with full configuration properties.
Tests using a Californium test client covering message types, content formats, error paths, and bus integration.
Write reference documentation (Asciidoc) with complete configuration property tables, defaults, and examples for the properties file used as the deployment manifest.
Stand up a MiniKDC-based kerberized HDFS mini-cluster for development and automated testing.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Implement secured Sqoop job support
activities.activity_description: Implement Kerberos authentication (keytab, JAAS, UserGroupInformation.doAs) and Sqoop job configuration changes so jobs run against the secured HDFS cluster.
Tests running Sqoop jobs against the secured cluster, covering successful auth, expired ticket re-login, and authorization failure paths.
Design the client API surface for the Diego Receptor REST API: resources, DTO model, authentication, and error model.
Implement the WebClient-based client covering Tasks, DesiredLRPs, ActualLRPs, Cells, and Domains endpoints, with DTOs, token auth, retries, and structured errors.
Tests against WireMock-stubbed Receptor API covering all endpoints, serialization, auth, and error handling.
Design the Spring Boot executable ModuleRunner replacing xd-containers, including module wiring and property binding approach.
Implement the Boot-based runner that bootstraps modules in container-managed environments without xd-containers, including lifecycle management and bus wiring.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Complete remaining deployment properties work
activities.activity_description: Complete the outstanding deployment properties support (instance count, resource limits, module-level overrides) and bind them via @ConfigurationProperties.
Integration tests launching representative modules through the Boot ModuleRunner, validating property binding and deployment behavior.
End-to-end testing across all stories (stateful streams with offset/state flushing, CoAP ingestion, secured Sqoop, receptor client, ModuleRunner) and regression verification.

activities.activity_name: Code review, refactoring, and defect fixing
activities.activity_description: Self-review against project standards, static analysis cleanup, refactoring, and fixing defects found during testing.
Update Maven build and CI pipelines for new modules and test profiles, package the increment, and finalize release notes.
